# odyssey-053 review, pass one (translation) — Odyssey 11.210–320

Reviewer pass one. `gloss.json` not read (pass two). `t` untouched (checked: units joined with a space reproduce the packet's 111 lines exactly; every `ln` and every `p` matches; `l` has the line division of `t` in every unit; no `\n` in any `i`; no ASCII apostrophe in `l` or `i`). Units 2 (11.215) and 24 (11.253) are character-identical to the published English. Quotation marks: Odysseus is narrating, so speeches carry single marks as in the shipped odyssey-043/049/052: Odysseus to his mother opens at 11.210 and closes at 11.214; the mother opens at 11.216 and closes at 11.224; Poseidon opens at 11.248 and closes at 11.252. Each has `mark` on its first unit. 11.210 correctly continues the introduction that ends odyssey-052's last unit (προσηύδων). No speech runs into the next part. Scansion flags: none in the packet, so nothing to add to notes.

Counts: 0 major, 3 moderate, 14 minor (17 edits).

## Considered and refused

- **11.213 ὤτρυν’ "has roused" in `l`/`i`** (aorist/imperfect, English perfect): a normal English rendering of a question about a present result; unit 7's note and `l` ("had roused") are consistent with it. Refused.
- **11.220 τὰ μέν τε "as always" in `l` only** (`i` drops it): `l` may carry the epic τε; the note names it a general-truth τε. Refused.
- **11.223 λιλαίεο `l` "long to go" vs `i` "be eager to reach"**: same sense. Refused.
- **11.231 `i` "I would not let them all"**: imperfect of resistance; the "would" is not a conditional. Refused.
- **11.233 προμνηστῖναι note says the sense is taken from context**: honest; kept.
- **11.238 note on ἐπ’ Ἐνιπῆος … ῥέεθρα (ἐπί + accusative)**: correct as written (Ἐνιπῆος is the possessive genitive). Refused.
- **11.239–248 `i` capital "But"/"She" after a semicolon in the previous unit** (e.g. unit 23, unit 14): the drafter starts a fresh English sentence where the Greek begins a new clause; `i` is allowed to restructure. Refused.
- **11.241 note "the more usual ἐνοσίχθων"**: the table and this part (252) both show it; kept.
- **11.251 `l` "your home" vs note "to the house"**: πρὸς δῶμα is "to (your) house"; `l`/`i` supply the possessive. Refused.
- **11.272 "Epicaste, whom later writers call Jocasta"**: about later writers, not about the poem; true. Refused.
- **11.276 διὰ between adjective and noun** called a preposition "between": correct. Refused.
- **11.289 note "ἀργαλέας is the stock ‘grievous’"**: the table fixes it; kept.
- **11.292 note "(as in ‘harsh old age’)"**: a back-reference to 11.196 that is true (shipped odyssey-052); kept.
- **11.298 ζωούς "standing in apposition"**: it is predicative, but the English ("both of whom, alive") shows the intended reading and "apposition" is a loose, not wrong, label. Refused.
- **11.311 measures in the note (45 cm, 1.8 m, four metres, sixteen)**: arithmetic checked (9 × 0.45 = 4.05; 9 × 1.8 = 16.2). Kept.
- **11.313–314 `i` "on Olympus" for ἐν Ὀλύμπῳ**: fine. Refused.
- **11.317 `i` omits νύ**: a weak particle; `l` carries "now indeed". Refused.
- **11.318 note "shows that it is Apollo"**: identification from the description alone; the part itself says Apollo is never named. Kept.
- **11.299 κρατερόφρονε**: checked: dual accusative, agrees with παῖδε, not with Τυνδαρέῳ (dative singular would be -ονι). The draft is right.
- **Table and formula checks**: all epithets follow the house table or the drafter's new-renderings rows (ἀμύμων, ἀγαυή, ἠύκομος, ἀντίθεος, ἱππόδαμος, τηλεκλειτός, ζείδωρος ἄρουρα, αἷμα κελαινόν, ὁπλοτάτην, αἰπύς, μένος αἰὲν ἀτειρής and the rest); no remembered English found in `i`.
- **Murray's numbering**: no irregularity in 11.210–320; the packet has 111 lines and no omission or transposition needs a note.

## Pass two: considered and refused

- **11.225 γυναῖκες** (known entry says ‘in apposition to δμωαί’): the parse ‘fem. nom. pl.’ is true of this use; no broadening needed.
- **11.257 Πύλῳ ἠμαθόεντι**: the known entry for πύλῳ says ‘fem. dat. sg.’ but ἠμαθόεντι shows the word masculine here; the new entry for ἠμαθόεντι says masc. An existing entry may not be rewritten, so it is left and recorded here.
- **11.243 purple**: the pass-one note ‘a dark, glossy colour’ is not false of πορφύρεος in general; changed only for consistency with the shipped wording of the same collocation (see above). `new-renderings.md` has no row for it and none was needed.
- **11.215, 11.253** (units 3, 25) and **11.230** (unit 10) are character-identical to the published English apart from the colon at 230, which the note explains.
- **11.219–224 `i` ‘keep all this in mind’ for ἴσθι**: the note says ‘take note of it, remember it’; consistent.
- **11.235 note ‘ἐύ ‘good’’** against the table’s ‘fair’ for ἐύ-: the new-renderings row fixes εὐπατέρεια as ‘well-fathered’, so ‘good’ is right for this word.
- **11.286 ἀγέρωχον** (‘lofty’): unknown, said so; kept.
- **11.292 ‘as in harsh old age’ and 11.230 ‘9.318’, 11.231 ‘10.439’, 11.247 ‘2.301–302’, 11.253 ‘4.570’**: each checked against the packet’s published-unit list; correct.
- **11.317 ἵκοντο ‘aorist indicative’**: correct (optative would be ἵκοιντο); kept from pass one.
- **ἐδύσετο gloss ‘she plunged’** and **ἤνασσε ‘aor.’**: older known entries, not rewritten; the parse (aor. mid. 3 sg. / past 3 sg.) is true of this use.
- **No remembered English found** in any `i`; no modern translation consulted.
